correlates.name: Renal Failure
correlates.pathophysiology: The kidneys are the sole effective route for neutralizing nonvolatile acid; when they fail, titratable buffer and ammonium excretion collapse and de novo bicarbonate generation stops.

correlates.name: Chronic Adrenal Insufficiency (Addison Disease)
correlates.presentation: Metabolic acidosis from acid retention, called life-threatening on the slide.
correlates.pathophysiology: Loss of glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid drive removes the stimulus for proximal Na+/H+ exchange and collecting duct H+ secretion, so acid is retained.

correlates.name: Acute Mountain Sickness (the Aspen vignette)
correlates.presentation: Throbbing headache, fatigue, nausea, shortness of breath, lightheadedness, difficulty focusing; worse on day two and with further ascent.
correlates.pathophysiology: Ascent lowers inspired PO2; hyperventilation lowers PaCO2 and raises blood pH into respiratory alkalosis, and renal compensation is too slow to help in the first days.
correlates.treatment: A carbonic anhydrase inhibitor (acetazolamide) started before the trip; ibuprofen only blunted the headache.

transporters.name: NBCe1 (Na+/HCO3- cotransporter)
transporters.location: Basolateral membrane of the proximal tubule
transporters.function: The exit door for reclaimed bicarbonate — it carries the HCO3- rebuilt inside the cell by carbonic anhydrase II back into the blood, completing reabsorption of the 4,320 mmol filtered each day
transporters.regulation: Upregulated along with NHE3 in chronic respiratory acidosis
transporters.inhibitor: Not directly blocked; the whole pathway stalls when carbonic anhydrase is inhibited

transporters.name: H+-ATPase (proton pump)
transporters.location: Apical membrane of type A (alpha) intercalated cells in the collecting duct
transporters.function: Actively secretes protons against a steep gradient, generating new bicarbonate — this is the step that titrates urinary buffers and can drive urine pH down to its floor of 4.4
transporters.regulation: Inserted acutely in respiratory acidosis; stimulated by angiotensin II and aldosterone
transporters.inhibitor: Its expression falls under mineralocorticoid receptor blockade, which is why K+-sparing agents alkalinize the urine

transporters.name: Pendrin (Cl-/HCO3- exchanger)
transporters.location: Apical membrane of type B (beta) intercalated cells in the collecting duct
transporters.function: Secretes bicarbonate into the lumen while reclaiming chloride — the reverse of the alpha cell, and the route by which the kidney corrects a metabolic alkalosis
transporters.regulation: The proportion of beta cells rises in metabolic alkalosis, and alpha cells can convert to beta cells

transporters.name: RhBG / RhCG (ammonia gas channels)
transporters.function: Move NH3 into the lumen, where secreted H+ traps it as NH4+ — diffusion trapping, the mechanism behind 40 of the 70 mmol of daily net acid excretion
transporters.regulation: Ammoniagenesis from glutamine rises in chronic metabolic acidosis and in hypokalemia
transporters.inhibitor: None; hyperkalemia competes with NH4+ in the medulla and blunts the pathway

transporters.name: Carbonic Anhydrase II and IV
transporters.location: CA II in the cytoplasm and CA IV anchored to the apical membrane of the proximal tubule (CA I lives in the red cell)
transporters.function: CA IV splits luminal H2CO3 to CO2 and water so the CO2 can diffuse in; CA II rebuilds HCO3- inside the cell and regenerates the H+ that NHE3 exports
transporters.regulation: Zinc-dependent and bidirectional, catalyzing the reaction in whichever direction the gradient runs
transporters.inhibitor: Sulfonamides — acetazolamide inhibits both isoforms, which is why bicarbonate reabsorption collapses

formulas.name: Net Acid Excretion
formulas.equation: Net acid excretion = titratable acid + NH4+ - excreted HCO3-
formulas.meaning: Reabsorbing filtered bicarbonate only returns the body to zero; new base is generated only by titrating a non-bicarbonate buffer such as phosphate, creatinine, urate or glutamine-derived ammonia
formulas.normalValue: About 70 mmol/day — 40 as NH4+ and 30 as titratable acid — matching the daily nonvolatile acid load

formulas.name: Daily Acid-Base Budget
formulas.equation: HCO3- filtered and reabsorbed 4,320 mmol/day; CO2 expired ~15,000 mmol/day; urinary H+ ~70 mmol/day
formulas.meaning: The scale gap is the whole point — plasma H+ is measured in nanomoles while filtered bicarbonate is measured in millimoles, so losing even a little filtered bicarbonate is catastrophic
formulas.normalValue: Arterial pH 7.37-7.42, equal to about 40 nEq/L of H+

formulas.name: Bicarbonate Reabsorption by Segment
formulas.equation: PCT 80%, thick ascending limb 10%, DCT 6%, medullary collecting duct 4%, urine 0.01%
formulas.meaning: Nearly all bicarbonate handling is reclamation in the proximal tubule; the distal nephron contributes little volume but does the regulated fine-tuning
formulas.normalValue: Minimum achievable urinary pH is 4.4 — free protons alone would require a pH of 1.3, which is why buffers are obligatory

formulas.name: The Four Acid-Base Disturbances
formulas.equation: Metabolic: HCO3- primary. Respiratory: pCO2 primary.
formulas.meaning: Metabolic acidosis lowers HCO3- and triggers hyperventilation; metabolic alkalosis raises it and triggers hypoventilation; respiratory disorders move pCO2 first and the kidney answers by adjusting bicarbonate reabsorption over days
formulas.normalValue: Normal values: pCO2 40 mmHg, pH 7.4, HCO3- 24 mEq/L

formulas.name: Renal Ammoniagenesis
formulas.equation: Glutamine to alpha-ketoglutarate yields 2 NH4+ plus new HCO3-
formulas.meaning: The proximal tubule makes both the buffer and the new base from one substrate; NH4+ then substitutes for K+ on NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb and is recycled into the medulla
formulas.normalValue: About 40 mmol/day of NH4+ excretion, rising sharply in chronic metabolic acidosis
